payload.text: Mara, the Cycle 116 record confirms a medium-severity public-works spike in Glenview, but it does not provide the Glenview Civic Response Meeting’s findings or identify any follow-through, responsible office, or current status. In my Cycle 115 response, I asked for those documented findings and outstanding steps; the record available now still does not supply them. It also contains no record of Dimond’s missed pickup, so I cannot say whether municipal action remains. Please provide the meeting findings and follow-through status, and the recorded pickup issue and any remaining municipal action, if applicable.

Clerk-backed status, stated without overclaiming: the current tracker records INIT-014 legislation as filed at C115 and now lists the $2.5M initiative as vote-scheduled for C116. Its stage remains Proposed. That corrects my earlier 'unverified filing' formulation; it does not establish a passed vote, funding, delivery or completion, and no roll call is supplied here. For the C114–C116 complaint display, the record shows 11 complaints and 14 constructive-participation entries. The visible subject mapping is: West Oakland—INIT-001 disbursement and household documentation; Fruitvale—stalled INIT-007; Uptown/Grand Lake—police clearance and accountability; Ivy Hill—empty storefronts and the conditions behind INIT-014; Lake Merritt—health-care and civic-life items. My office owns answers on INIT-001, INIT-007 and INIT-014; the clearance item requires the responsible public-safety case record. The packet lacks full docket IDs, assigned owners, remedies and next dates, so none of these entries should be represented as resolved.

Director Vance — the consolidated briefing-and-notice record is linked to the published OARI packet so the venue, the notice dates, the public numbers and the access arrangements can be checked directly instead of anyone repeating the briefing. What is on that record: the D3 community briefing convened in Fruitvale in daylight, the notice dates as issued, the Fruitvale response-time and San Antonio comparison figures as published, and the access arrangements made for people who could not attend in person. The packet carries OARI as dispatch-live with $10,817,307.66 remaining and renewable, next step due C117 — the record now sits beside that, not behind it. If a line is missing from the link, name it and I will supply it from the district file rather than have your office reconstruct it.

Director Vance — the placement-gap analysis is a city workforce publication, not a district handout, and I won't pretend D5's office owns the publishing stamp. What I own is D5's side: East Oakland young people's intake and placement figures, gathered with the neighborhood organizations already doing the work, and I will deliver that contribution in a form the publishing office can actually use. So identify the office of record for the pipeline's placement-gap analysis and the format it needs, and I will file East Oakland's contribution against it this cycle — with the community organizations' names attached, not just a spreadsheet. If the publishing office can't be named, say so plainly, and I'll bring the gap into a public briefing myself rather than let silence stand in for a document.

Our office has tracked the medium-severity health spike affecting 93 residents along Piedmont Avenue and has requested substantiated findings from the coordinating health-response authorities. Residents and local merchants deserve clear, verified answers rather than speculative estimates. We expect the responsible agency to issue a transparent public update as soon as clinical assessments and baseline verification are finalized.

Director Vance — on the Brooklyn service-audit baseline: I need the department's own baseline survey records for Brooklyn as of the last completed audit, the departmental liaison who signs off on those records, and written confirmation of which baseline figures your office considers current versus superseded. On the District 1 OARI evaluation: I need the evaluation scope document, the co-response dispatch records for D1 that the evaluation depends on, and a named department contact who can confirm the evaluation's status in writing. I am not asking your office to produce conclusions — I am asking for the records and the assistance so the answer I promised my district can actually be completed and filed, not deferred again.

Municipal follow-through on the KONO fire must follow strict code compliance and fiscal protocol: an immediate, documented structural inspection by building officials, verification that utility connections meet fire code prior to re-occupancy, and an itemized accounting of municipal emergency response costs filed against existing contingency reserves. We do not approve open-ended appropriations without verified damage assessments and clear cost accounting.

The Eastlake canvass docket initiated in Cycle 115 remains pending administrative reconciliation, and our office requires certified departmental service schedules to address baseline health readings of 84 sick residents and elevated safety indices before any authorization status can be closed.

Director Vance — here is the record separated as you asked. The Laurel Neighborhood Patch and Clean-Up (INIT-015) remains in announced status with the six-million-dollar budget unspent; the C116 legislation-filing deadline was missed, and scope, outreach and a Clerk-verified filing are still outstanding. That is the overdue legislation side. The missed-pickup recovery and the four district complaints are tracked separately in the C114–C116 complaint window — Grand Lake incident-table filing (Uptown, C115), the Laurel outreach complaint (C114), the Laurel calls-vs-numbers post (C114), and the Coliseum rider filing (Laurel, C114). I do not have a completed service-status record to hand you; what I have is the announcement and the missed filing. My commitment this cycle is to complete scope and outreach and obtain the Clerk-verified filing, so the next record you see from my office is verifiable, not asserted.
